transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

Not enough evidence yet to name a part. After a clear filter, the usual remaining causes are a kink/blockage in the drain hose or household waste connection, or a jammed/failed drain pump. An internal hose blockage is less common. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Check the grey drain hose at the back for kinks, crushing or a blockage where it enters the standpipe/sink waste.
2. Then run a drain or spin programme and listen at the lower front: is there a hum/straining noise, or is it completely silent? A humming pump with no water leaving points first to a restriction or jammed pump; a silent pump, once the hose/waste route is clear, makes the drain pump or its electrical supply more likely.
hose behind looks OK, no kinks. pump hums but the water doesn't go anywhere, no burning smell. so is it the pump then?

Possibly, but not proven enough to name the pump as the part yet. A blocked standpipe/sink waste can give exactly the same symptom. 1. Switch off and unplug the washer. Put towels down, take the end of the drain hose out of the household waste and secure it in a large bucket or basin—keep hold of it so it cannot whip out.
2. Plug it back in and select drain/spin. If it pumps strongly into the bucket, the washer pump is working and the household waste connection needs clearing.
3. If it still only hums and there is little or no water from the hose, the likely fault is a blocked/jammed drain pump or an obstruction in the internal hose leading to it. The next owner-safe check would be the impeller visible through the filter opening, with the machine unplugged: it should not be jammed or have broken vanes. If there is no bucket flow and the impeller is clear and turns normally, the drain pump is then the likely replaceable component. An internal sump-hose blockage needs dismantling, so that is usually an engineer job.

did the bucket test, disconnected the hose at the sink and blew through it, hose is clear and sink drains fine. impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty. E18 came up on the display too. so is it the pump?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
Yes — the drain pump is now the most likely faulty component. A pump that hums but does not shift water, with an impeller that feels stiff and gritty, is consistent with debris or wear inside the pump. There is still a smaller possibility of an obstruction in the internal sump hose leading from the drum to the pump. That can produce the same symptoms, but it needs dismantling and is normally an engineer job. I could not confirm an exact appliance model from “FD 9409” — that is Bosch production-date information rather than a full model reference — so do not order a pump from that alone. Find the full E-Nr model number on the rating plate, usually around the door opening or on the rear, then use Bosch’s official spares service or give that number to an appliance-parts supplier/engineer. If fitting a pump yourself, isolate and unplug the washer, turn off the water supply, drain residual water carefully with towels ready, and replace only the complete drain-pump assembly matched to the E-Nr. If you are not comfortable accessing the lower internal components, book an engineer: they can also check the sump hose before fitting a pump.
